title: Disabling tracking on a stocked part shows the Disable tracking confirmation
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Parts -> Inventory page on the build under test, with permission to view inventory parts.
  2. You hold the "Part Library & Inventory - Delete" permission (needed to change status/tracking).
  3. A tracked part holding more than zero on hand (e.g. 5 EA across its bins).
custom_steps:
1. In Edit Inventory Part, turn tracking off.
  2. Read the confirmation title, its statement of how many units the part holds, and that turning off clears every bin's quantity.
  3. Check the dialog is the standard one (title, message, Cancel, confirm - no field to type into) and read the confirm button.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Turning tracking off on a part holding more than zero shows a confirmation before anything changes, titled "Disable tracking?", stating how many units the part holds and that turning tracking off will clear the quantity in every bin location.
  • It is the application's standard confirmation dialog (title, message, Cancel, confirm button, nothing to type; confirm available at once); the confirm button reads "Disable tracking", styled destructive, with Cancel beside it.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; "Parts Lifecycle Update" PRD (Confluence 829227015, IN REVIEW 2026-09-09), Story 5 (Edit tracking state); design canvas Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026 against an IN-REVIEW spec; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-E1: “If the user turns tracking off on a part that holds more than zero on hand, a confirmation appears before anything changes.”
  • S5-E2: “The confirmation states how many units the part currently holds.”
  • S5-E3: “The confirmation states that turning tracking off will clear the quantity in every bin location.”
  • S5-E3a: “The confirmation is titled "Disable tracking?".”
  • S5-E4: “The confirmation is the application's standard confirmation dialog, the same one every other destructive action in the product uses. It carries a title, the message, a Cancel and a confirm button, and nothing else. There is no field to type into and nothing to transcribe: the confirm button is available as soon as the dialog opens.”
  • S5-E4a: “The confirm button reads Disable tracking and is styled as a destructive action. Cancel sits beside it, in the position the standard dialog puts it.”
